title: memory leak
concept: If delete is omitted, heap memory will not be freed until the program ends.

steps.title: Enter leaky function
steps.explanation: The `leaky()` function is called, creating a new stack frame.

steps.title: Allocate on heap
steps.explanation: Allocate memory on the heap with `new int(999)` and store the address in pointer `p`.

steps.title: Function exits — leak!
steps.explanation:
When `leaky()` finishes, the pointer `p` disappears along with the stack frame.

But since we didn't call `delete`, **999 of the heap remains**. There is no way to access this memory — this is a **memory leak**.

quiz.question: What causes memory leaks?
options: If you do not delete the memory allocated on the heap and lose the pointer,
quiz.explanation: Memory allocated on the heap must be explicitly freed with delete. When a pointer goes out of scope, there is no way to access that memory.

misconceptions.wrong: When the program ends, all memory is automatically released.
misconceptions.correct: Although the operating system reclaims it when the process terminates, the leak can be critical on long-running servers.
misconceptions.why: If the leak repeats, there will be less and less available memory, causing the system to slow down or crash.

keyTakeaway: If you allocate with new, be sure to free it with delete. A better way is to use smart pointers.
